instruction: Make the second slide's title say "Details" and center it.

metadata.explanation: Task variation 5: Center alignment with title 'Details' on slide 2. Verified slide 2 (index 1) exists and currently has empty title. Evaluator checks both alignment (CENTER) and text (Details) with partial credit scoring.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for correct alignment (CENTER), 0.5 for correct text (Details)

llm_judge_reasons: Critical getter logic flaw: Getter finds title by checking 'first non-empty text shape' (impress.py:44-47), but this will FAIL if the title is empty or if there are other text shapes on the slide
The getter does not properly identify the title placeholder using shape.is_placeholder or placeholder_format.type, so it may grab subtitle or body text instead of the actual title
Metadata states 'slide 2 (index 1) exists and currently has empty title', but getter logic requires shape.text.strip() to be truthy (line 44), which will skip empty titles entirely
After task completion, if slide has multiple text shapes, the getter may not consistently identify the title shape - it just grabs the first one with text
The title detection logic is semantically incorrect for PowerPoint/Impress slide structure - it should check placeholder types, not text content presence
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Rewrite getter to properly identify title placeholder: check shape.is_placeholder and shape.placeholder_format.type == PP_PLACEHOLDER.TITLE (or equivalent for python-pptx)
Remove the text.strip() requirement (line 44) so the getter can find titles even when empty
Use slide.shapes.title property if available in python-pptx, which directly accesses the title placeholder
If using generic shape iteration, check for placeholder type first, then fall back to position-based heuristics (top-most text shape)
Handle the case where title placeholder exists but is empty - should still return alignment and empty text, not None values
